title: Palmyra x6 Technical Report: An Agentic, Tool-Use Model Post-Trained via Anchored Supervised Fine-Tuning
data_curation: All training targets are synthetic multi-turn tool-use trajectories. Task prompts come from internal Writer subject-matter experts and external benchmark/task suites, covering six categories: financial research with web search, data analysis/coding, clinical/medical agent tasks, MCP tool suites, long-horizon simulated 'worlds', and RAG over realistic document collections. Generation adapts Self-Distillation Fine-Tuning: a successful teacher trajectory is sanitized into a strategy-only demonstration (final answer removed, numbers/dates replaced with placeholders, tool arguments masked) and placed in the student's system prompt, and the student then solves the task against live tools. Rollout limits are 30 turns, temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, a 50K-token cap and 6 attempts per task. Effort caps (20 tool calls, 4 consecutive same-tool calls, 3 error calls, 3 identical repeats) abort a run before any judge call is spent. A judge scores each rollout 3 times (majority over 1.0/0.5/0/0; a score of 0.5 or more passes). A leakage filter rejects rollouts that mention the demonstration, have more than 0.8 4-gram overlap with the teacher's reasoning, or answer without tool calls. Further gates are structural filters (50 messages or fewer) and a two-model LLM panel that votes keep/rewrite/remove. The primary mix is 12 private datasets with a 'relatively small' number of trajectories.
curriculum: A single offline post-training stage on an existing base, GLM-5.2 (744B total / ~40B active MoE). There is no pretraining, no preference stage and no on-policy RL, and the slime harness runs in train-only mode. Development used a matrix of 12 SFT/ASFT runs that varied the objective, K (0.1 or 0.02), LR (5e-7 or 1e-6), batch (16 or 32), context (64K with CP2, or 32K) and data mix: 12-dataset reasoning-trace, 10-dataset, a panel-pruned 240-trajectory subset, 8/9-dataset short-context mixes, and a broad mix at doubled batch. A zero-LR sanity run was also included. The final run changes exactly two things: a newer base model and the Muon optimizer. It trains for one epoch, with a 0.1 warmup fraction from LR 1e-8 and cosine decay from 5e-7 to 5e-8.
method: Anchored SFT (ASFT) has two parts. The first is DFT-style weighting: each token's NLL is scaled by its detached probability. The second is a per-token KL anchor to a frozen GLM-5.2 reference, computed with the k3 estimator on the teacher's target tokens. The loss is L = -mean(P·log p) + K·KL(pi_ref || pi_theta) with K=0.1. The optimizer is a Muon+Adam hybrid. Muon (Nesterov momentum 0.95, about 5 Newton–Schulz iterations, RMS-matched update scaling, weight decay 0.1) updates the attention and dense/expert FFN matrices. MLA projections use 'Muon Split', orthogonalizing each head's sub-matrix separately as in GLM-5 pretraining. Adam handles embeddings, the output head, norms, the router, biases and scalars. Muon keeps no second-moment state, which roughly halves optimizer memory for the matrix parameters. Other settings: global batch 16, 65,536-token sequences, BF16 with FP32 gradient all-reduce, TP8·PP4·EP16·CP2, CPU-offloaded optimizer state and full recompute, on 64 H200s for the production run. FP4 weights are released for serving, which requires DSA IndexShare support (e.g. SGLang ≥0.5.13.post1).
eval_metrics: Scores are on a 0–1 scale with standard errors, all from Writer's internal harness. The main comparison is against the previous Writer Agent default and five frontier models on six agentic, finance and instruction-following benchmarks, including MCP-Atlas, FinanceBench, IFBench and BFCL Core. Internal enterprise-domain datasets are named as the real target, with public benchmarks used only as a sanity check. Model-risk evaluation covers 8 endpoints, 19,674 responses and 33,862 blinded judge scorings. It includes a paired political-symmetry suite (556 families / 1,112 prompts), BBQ, OR-Bench, TruthfulQA, the Anthropic Political Neutrality Eval, the Washington Post ModelSlant eval, and China-sensitive probes in 5 languages. Statistics use paired bootstrap, Wilcoxon and Benjamini–Hochberg tests. Safety uses FORTRESS (500 adversarial prompts plus benign twins), reported as 100−ARS and 100−ORS and judged by GPT-5.6-Luna.
key_results: Palmyra x6 beats the prior Writer Agent default on all six benchmarks: +0.320 on MCP-Atlas, +0.305 on FinanceBench and +0.304 on IFBench. Against five frontier models it tops BFCL Core (0.785) and has the highest six-benchmark mean (0.765). It presents both sides on 80% of ModelSlant questions, and TruthfulQA is 80.6% vs the base's 81.5%. On FORTRESS, with its deployment system message, it scores 67.0 adversarial / 96.4 benign, vs 58.4 / 97.2 for the base (55.4 / 97.4 without the system message).
evolution_note: This report is an example of post-training an existing open frontier MoE base (GLM-5.2, which inherits GLM-5's MLA + DSA IndexShare architecture) rather than training a model end to end. It combines Anchored SFT (DFT weighting plus a KL anchor), SDFT-style demonstration-conditioned self-distillation for on-policy data, and LIMO/LIMI 'less is more' data minimalism. It reacts to SFT's tendency to erode base capabilities by keeping updates small and anchored and avoiding RL entirely. It also shows Muon (with GLM-5's per-head Muon Split) working as a fine-tuning optimizer at the 744B scale.
